reading.identification: A shallow lean-to annex (one of the former penshuizekens) attached to the flank of the early-15th-century Groot Vleeshuis on Pensmarkt, Ghent: a 2.5 m deep stone service range with a wide timber cart gate at ground level, currently under restoration.
reading.notes:
Wall enum has no stone entry; the facade is grey Tournai limestone (Doornikse kalksteen) in coursed blocks over a lighter ashlar plinth, so I chose marble as the closest dielectric proxy (eps ~7) rather than concrete or brick. Some darker brick infill is visible in the upper wall between the hall's dormers, but the annex's own street face reads as stone throughout. Roughness 7 mm covers weathered coursed masonry with recessed and partly eroded joints - this is the 1-10 cm regime and must stay a scattering parameter, not geometry.

Height 9.0 m is height_source=no-data, i.e. a fallback. I split it 4.5/4.5 over two storeys so the generator lands on the stated total, but the annex as photographed reads as one tall gated storey plus a wall zone rising to the hall eaves. Treat the storey split as a rhythm hint, not a measurement.

The steep blue-slate pitch with stone crow-stepped dormer gablets that dominates both street photos belongs to the Vleeshuis hall itself, a different and much larger polygon. Do not attach it to this 32 m2 sliver. This building gets the low slate mono-pitch visible directly above the timber gate, sloping down toward the street with its high edge against the hall wall.

Both photos are a restoration snapshot. The yellow raking props, the crane, and the white picket hoarding are temporary and must not be baked into the twin. The correct permanent clutter for Pensmarkt is pedestrian: car_access=none on a highway=pedestrian, so no parked or moving vehicles anywhere on this frontage. Waste bins, A-boards, bollards and market stalls against the plinth are appropriate; a terrace is not, since this face is service frontage rather than cafe frontage.

Detail budget: spend it on the gate reveal, the plinth string course, the window reveals and sills, and the eaves line of the lean-to, all of which are above 10 cm and are what the 28 GHz beam actually resolves at street level. The upper hall wall is largely occluded from the corridor and deserves less.
